description.narrative: IFC is providing a financing package of up to US$20 million to South Asia Gateway Terminals (SAGT), to finance the purchase of new ship-to-shore cranes. The investment could potentially include Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) and the balance would come from a parallel lender. These crane upgrades will support SAGT's competitiveness, productivity, and reduce fuel consumption and emissions. South Asia Gateway Terminals (Private) Limited (SAGT) is Sri Lanka's first public-private partnership international container terminal, operating at the Port of Colombo under a 30-year build-operate-transfer (BOT) concession awarded in 1999 by the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA). IFC was one of the original financiers, providing a US$35 million loan and US$7.3 million equity investment in 1999. SAGT is one of the five terminals operating at the Port of Colombo, a key transhipment hub for South Asia that serves India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and the Maldives.

Potential outcomes include improved quality of port services through the modernization of quayside equipment, which will enhance efficiency in container handling. Beyond the project, the investment is expected to enhance the competitiveness of Sri Lanka's maritime industry by sustaining Port of Colombo's regional and global trade integration. The Project is also expected to improve the sector's sustainability by enhancing access to sustainable finance.
